events.text: In the Hwangbo hall over the lake, every child of the house is rowed across the nine crossings before its fourth spring, so the water learns its name. Today the boat is yours, and the old ferry spearman stands in the bow.

choices.text: Hold the gunwale and watch the water

effects.log: You do not cry once. The ferry spearman tells the hall the lake has accepted you.

choices.text: Grab the ferry pole and try to push

effects.log: You nearly go over the side. Everyone laughs, and an aunt says you have the Hwangbo arms.

choices.text: Fall asleep on the spearman's coat

effects.log: You sleep through all nine crossings. The spearman says the best ferrymen do.

events.text: At dawn the children of the house stand on the wet jetty with reed poles and practise the Reed Crossing Spear until the poles snap. Aunt Ok-ran, the spear-mistress of the house, does not let anyone stop before the sun clears the mist.

choices.text: Drill until the pole breaks

ok.log: Your pole snaps first. Aunt Ok-ran hands you a real spear without a word.

fail.log: Your hands blister before the pole does. You keep going anyway.

choices.text: Watch how the aunt shifts her feet on the wet boards

effects.log: The spear starts in the heel, not the hand. You see it before the others do.

choices.text: Help the ferrymen tie up the morning boats

effects.log: The ferrymen teach you knots and lake songs. They will remember who helped.

events.text: A Water Gang barge has run the Hwangbo crossing at night without paying the old toll, and its captain sends word that the lakes belong to whoever has the boats. The elders look at you.

choices.text: Wait for the barge at the crossing with a spear

ok.log: The captain goes into the lake and the barge pays twice. The hall drinks to your name tonight.

fail.log: He knocks you off the jetty with an oar. The barge goes by laughing, and the elders say nothing.

choices.text: Row out and argue the old charters with him

ok.log: You read him the charter of three dynasties. He pays, sour, and the Gang keeps to the toll a while.

fail.log: He cannot read and does not care to. The barge goes on, and the toll is a story.

choices.text: Let it pass; the lake is wide

effects.log: The elders call it weakness. Some of the ferrymen call it sense.

events.text: The Wudang Taoists cross the lake every spring to the Hwangbo hall to drink tea and argue about the soft and the hard. This year the head of the house sends you to sit at their table.

choices.text: Argue that the spear is the river and not the stone

ok.log: An old Taoist laughs and concedes. He says the Hwangbo have finally sent someone who listens.

fail.log: They take your argument apart gently, one cup at a time. You learn more losing.

choices.text: Pour the tea and keep quiet

effects.log: You pour well and say nothing. The Taoists ask after you by name the next spring.

choices.text: Spar with their youngest disciple on the jetty

effects.log: Neither of you falls in. You part friends, and the house's old friendship holds.

events.text: The head of the Hwangbo Clan is grey now, and at the spring rite the whole house waits for the name of the heir. Two cousins have been standing a little straighter all year. Your own name has been spoken too.

choices.text: Put yourself forward at the rite

ok.log: The head of the house looks at you a long time and nods. Your name goes on the heir's tablet beside the lake.

fail.log: The head names a cousin. The hall looks at you to see what you will do. You bow.

choices.text: Speak for the cousin who held the crossings in the flood

effects.log: The hall remembers that you spoke for the house, not for yourself.

choices.text: Stay out of it and keep to the jetty

effects.log: The rite ends, a name is spoken, and the spears are drilled the next morning as always.

events.text: Every child of the Moyong is given a ledger on its fifth birthday, bound in indigo silk, with one line already written in it: the first kindness the house has done for them. Yours is handed to you over a bowl of sweet rice.

choices.text: Ask what the line says

effects.log: Your grandmother reads it aloud: a doctor fetched through a winter flood the night you were born. You never forget it.

choices.text: Write your own first line in it, badly

effects.log: You draw a crooked character for thank you. The stewards frame the page.

choices.text: Try to trade the ledger for a sugar figure

effects.log: The sugar seller refuses, horrified. The whole house hears of it and laughs for a year.

events.text: The Moyong practise the Nine-Bend Canal Sword on the stone bridges over the dye canals, where one bad step drops you into a vat of indigo. Uncle Seok, the swordmaster of the house, wears white to prove he never falls.

choices.text: Cross all nine bridges in the form

ok.log: You finish the ninth bend dry. Uncle Seok raises one eyebrow, which counts as praise.

fail.log: You come out of the vat blue to the elbows, and stay blue for a week.

choices.text: Study how the canal bends before the bridge

effects.log: The sword turns where the water turns. Everything in Jiangnan is a lesson.

choices.text: Count the stewards' ledgers with the clerks instead

effects.log: You learn where the house's silver goes. The clerks say you have the Moyong head for it.

events.text: The Hwangbo of Hubei have raised the toll at their lake crossings, and three Moyong silk barges sit idle behind their chain. The head of the house wants it settled without a war, and with nothing written down.

choices.text: Go up the river and duel their champion at the chain

ok.log: The spearman yields at the third exchange. The chain comes down, and your name goes in the ledger as a kindness owed.

fail.log: His spear is longer than your patience. You come home with a bruise and the barges still waiting.

choices.text: Buy their steward a dinner and learn what he owes

ok.log: By the third course he owes the Moyong rather a lot. The chain comes down the next morning.

fail.log: He eats well and promises nothing. The house writes his name in the other column.

choices.text: Send the silk the long way round by road

effects.log: It costs a month and a good deal of silver. The house writes the slight down.

events.text: A Tang envoy comes down the river with a lacquered box: the Tang wish to buy Moyong indigo for their winter robes, and to talk, quietly, about a match between the houses. The head of the house sends you to receive him.

choices.text: Bargain for the indigo like a merchant

ok.log: The envoy pays more than he meant and thanks you for it. The friendship of the two houses grows warmer.

fail.log: He gets the indigo cheap. The head of the house sighs and writes it down as a kindness done.

choices.text: Speak of the match, and of nothing else

effects.log: The envoy smiles. Letters will go up the river all winter, and some of them will be about you.

choices.text: Show him the dye works and the canals

effects.log: He leaves impressed and a little blue at the fingers. The houses stay friends.

events.text: The head of the Moyong has written the name of the heir in the great ledger and sealed the page. It will be opened at the autumn rite. Until then, every steward in the house is very polite to you, just in case.

choices.text: Open the ledger yourself the night before

ok.log: Your own name is on the page. You seal it again so well nobody ever knows.

fail.log: An aunt catches you with the seal in your hand. She says nothing, and writes it down.

choices.text: Wait for the rite like everyone else

effects.log: At the rite the page is read, and the house goes on as it always has: patiently.

choices.text: Pay every debt you owe before the rite

effects.log: Whatever the page says, nobody in Jiangnan can say a Moyong owes them.

events.text: The Sima keep the muster rolls of every garrison on the frontier, and every child of the house is written into the great roll on its sixth winter, with its height, its voice and the way it holds a bow. Today it is your turn.

choices.text: Draw the child's bow as far as it goes

effects.log: The string slaps your wrist and you do not let go. The clerk writes: steady.

choices.text: Answer the clerk's questions very loudly

effects.log: The whole hall hears you. The clerk writes: a voice for the drums.

choices.text: Ask to read what the roll says about your grandfather

effects.log: The clerk lets you. Two lines, cold and exact. You decide yours will be longer.

events.text: From the beacon tower above the Sima hall the children shoot at a straw rider dragged across the steppe a long bowshot away. Uncle Dal, the bowmaster, counts every arrow aloud, and twice.

choices.text: Hit the rider at the far end

ok.log: Your arrow takes the straw rider in the shoulder. Uncle Dal counts it twice, and nods.

fail.log: Your arrows go into the grass. Uncle Dal counts them twice anyway, aloud.

choices.text: Watch the wind in the grass before every shot

effects.log: The steppe tells you where the arrow will go. Count twice, shoot once.

choices.text: Help the old drummer keep the tower's time

effects.log: You learn the beacon drum. Every garrison on the frontier knows that beat.

events.text: A Jegal strategist has published a treatise saying the Sima lost the last frontier war by their own counting. Copies are in every teahouse in the north. The head of the house wants an answer worth remembering.

choices.text: Challenge the strategist to a game of war on the sand table

ok.log: You take his last banner in forty moves before a hall full of officers. The treatise is not reprinted.

fail.log: He takes yours in thirty. He is very polite about it, which is worse.

choices.text: Write a reply from the muster rolls, numbers and all

effects.log: Your reply is dry, exact and devastating. The north argues about it for a year.

choices.text: Let it go; the house plans in decades

effects.log: The head of the house writes the strategist's name in a small book. The Sima are patient.

events.text: The Paeng ride in from the steppe for the autumn muster, loud and dusty, and the two houses eat together in the long hall as they have for a hundred years. A Paeng cousin challenges you to an arm-wrestle across the table.

choices.text: Take the challenge

ok.log: You win, narrowly. The Paeng roar with delight and pour you three cups of tea in a row.

fail.log: You lose, narrowly. The Paeng roar with delight anyway. They like you better for trying.

choices.text: Talk muster and horses with the Paeng elders

effects.log: You learn where their riders will be next spring. The houses ride together for a reason.

choices.text: Count the Paeng horses for the roll, as a courtesy

effects.log: The Paeng are touched. Nobody has ever counted their horses so carefully.

events.text: The head of the Sima has asked every grown child of the house for a written plan: how the frontier should be held for the next thirty years. The best plan will name the heir. Yours lies blank on the table.

choices.text: Write the plan through the night

ok.log: The head of the house reads yours twice, then once more. Your name is added to the great roll as heir.

fail.log: Your plan is good. A cousin's is better. You read it, and admit it.

choices.text: Write a plan that serves whoever is chosen

effects.log: It names no heir and every garrison. The head of the house keeps it on the desk.

choices.text: Hand in the blank page

effects.log: The house is puzzled. The head of the house is not: some people are not made for the roll.

events.text: When a Gongsun child is old enough to climb the lighthouse stairs alone, it lights the great lamp for the first time while the whole harbour watches. Tonight the stairs are yours, all three hundred of them.

choices.text: Climb all the way without stopping

effects.log: You arrive red-faced and light the lamp. Every ship in the harbour rings its bell for you.

choices.text: Stop and count the ships from every window

effects.log: You count forty-one. The harbour master says it was forty, and checks, and it was forty-one.

choices.text: Let the old lamp-keeper carry you the last flight

effects.log: She says she has carried three generations of the house up those stairs. The lamp burns just as bright.

events.text: The Gongsun learn the Anchor Chain Fist in the shipyard, hauling the great chains hand over hand while Aunt Bo-ri, the yard-mistress, beats time on an iron bollard and shouts insults at the sea.

choices.text: Haul the heaviest chain

ok.log: The anchor comes up out of the water and the shipwrights cheer. Aunt Bo-ri calls you a small whale.

fail.log: The chain wins. You sit in the mud and Aunt Bo-ri insults the chain for you.

choices.text: Learn the shipwrights' songs while you haul

effects.log: You learn that the chain moves on the beat, not on the muscle.

choices.text: Mend nets with the old sailors at the end of the jetty

effects.log: They tell you stories of every pirate the house has sunk. Some are true.

events.text: A Gongsun lamp-keeper is found asleep at the foot of the lighthouse with a black thread around his wrist: the mark of the Hushed Lantern Pavilion. Someone wanted the lamp dark tonight, and a ship is due.

choices.text: Climb the tower and hold it till dawn

ok.log: The shadow on the stairs meets you and goes back down the outside of the tower. The lamp burns all night.

fail.log: You wake on the stairs at dawn. The lamp is dark. The ship came in safe by luck alone.

choices.text: Ring the harbour bell and wake the whole house

effects.log: Half the clan comes up the stairs with lanterns. Nobody tries the tower tonight.

choices.text: Light the lamp and leave the shadows alone

effects.log: The lamp burns. Whatever was on the stairs is gone by morning.

events.text: The beggars of the harbour towns have eaten at the Gongsun kitchen door every winter for a hundred years. This winter their elder comes in person, with news of pirates gathering off the islands.

choices.text: Sit with the beggar elder at the head table

effects.log: The house is scandalised, then proud. The Beggars' Sect will hear every rumour of the sea for you now.

choices.text: Sail out to look at the islands yourself

ok.log: You find the pirate anchorage and slip away unseen. The house strikes first that spring.

fail.log: A squall turns you back. You come home soaked and none the wiser.

choices.text: Send the beggars home with salt and rice (10 taels)

effects.log: Ten sacks go out of the kitchen door. The news keeps coming in.

events.text: The head of the Gongsun has called the house to the shipyard: the heir will be the one who launches the new flagship, and the slipway is greased. Three cousins and you stand by the ropes.

choices.text: Cut the rope and run the ship into the sea

ok.log: The ship goes down the slipway straight and true. The harbour rings every bell. Your name is painted on the stern.

fail.log: The ship sticks halfway. A cousin frees it with one heave, and the bells ring for her.

choices.text: Hand the axe to the cousin who built the hull

effects.log: The shipwrights never forget it. Neither does the cousin.

choices.text: Watch from the lighthouse with the lamp-keeper

effects.log: From up here every heir looks small, and the sea looks the same.

events.text: Duanmu children are taught the names of the hundred herbs on the tea terraces before they are taught their letters. This morning your grandmother walks you up the terrace with a basket and a riddle for every plant.

choices.text: Guess every riddle

effects.log: You get nine of ten. The tenth is the one that heals and kills, and she says that one takes a lifetime.

choices.text: Eat a leaf to see what it does

effects.log: Your tongue goes numb for an hour. Your grandmother laughs and names the leaf. You never forget it.

choices.text: Carry the basket for her all the way up

effects.log: At the top she gives you the first leaf of the season to keep.

events.text: In the clinic hall the young of the house practise the Mist-Valley Needle on a bronze figure pierced with three hundred points. Uncle Il, the needle-master, fills it with water: a true point lets one drop through.

choices.text: Find the points one by one

ok.log: Water beads at every point you touch. Uncle Il says your hands were born for the needle.

fail.log: The figure stays dry. Uncle Il says the bronze is patient, and so must you be.

choices.text: Help in the clinic with the real patients

effects.log: Mule drivers, a fevered child, a monk with a bad knee. You learn more in a day than in a month at the figure.

choices.text: Gather mist-valley moss for the medicines

effects.log: Wet, cold work in the gorge. The pharmacy keeps your name in its book.

events.text: A caravan comes up the tea road with six mule drivers poisoned, and the poison is one the house knows: a Ten Thousand Poison Valley brew, sold to whoever pays. Their dealer is drinking at the inn below.

choices.text: Cure the drivers first, all night

ok.log: All six live. By dawn the whole tea road knows the Duanmu undid the Valley's brew.

fail.log: Four live. You sit with the other two till the end, and the house buries them with honour.

choices.text: Go down to the inn and face the dealer

ok.log: He does not leave the inn on his own feet. The Valley's brew stops coming up the tea road.

fail.log: He throws powder in your face and is gone into the mist. Your eyes sting for days.

choices.text: Write down the brew for the house's books

effects.log: Every antidote the Duanmu know began this way: with patience.

events.text: The Five Poisons Sect sends a silver-hung envoy up the terraces: a sickness is in their villages that their own cures cannot touch, and the old friendship of healer and poisoner is called upon.

choices.text: Go down into the jungle with the envoy

ok.log: You find the sickness in the well water. The villages live, and the Five Poisons swear to remember it.

fail.log: You slow the sickness but cannot end it. The envoy thanks you anyway; you came.

choices.text: Trade them herbs for their antidote secrets

effects.log: You come home with three antidotes the house never knew. Both sides think they got the better of it.

choices.text: Send the house's best needles with the envoy (15 taels)

effects.log: The needles go down the terraces in a lacquered case. The friendship holds.

events.text: The head of the Duanmu is ill, and will not be treated by anyone but the one who will be heir. The house waits to see who the head will allow to take the pulse.

choices.text: Take the pulse and name the illness

ok.log: You name it, and treat it, and the head of the house gets up from the sickbed and names you heir.

fail.log: You name the wrong illness. A cousin names the right one. The head of the house smiles at you both.

choices.text: Bring the best physician of the cousins to the bedside

effects.log: The patient comes first. The house says it is the most Duanmu thing anyone has done in years.

choices.text: Sit outside the door and keep the house quiet

effects.log: Somebody has to. The terraces are very still for a week.

events.text: On the seventh day of the new year every child of the Yue writes the first character of its name in the great book of the house, with the brush of the founder. Your grandfather holds the inkstone, and your hand.

choices.text: Write it in one stroke, no blot

effects.log: A small, shaky, unbroken stroke. Your grandfather says the founder would have signed it.

choices.text: Write it very large

effects.log: It takes half a page. The house laughs, and keeps the page open for a month.

choices.text: Ask why the brush is so old

effects.log: He tells you about the founder until the candle goes out. You fall asleep with ink on your cheek.

events.text: The Yue practise the Eight Strokes Sword with brushes before they touch steel: each form is a stroke of a character, written in water on the courtyard stones. Aunt Min-ji, the sword-scholar of the house, reads every one.

choices.text: Write the whole character in one breath

ok.log: The water dries on the stones in a perfect character. Aunt Min-ji hands you a sword.

fail.log: Your character has a blot. Aunt Min-ji says a blot in water dries; a blot in steel does not. Again.

choices.text: Copy the classics in the library instead

effects.log: You copy until your wrist aches. The strokes of the sword are in every page.

choices.text: Walk to the canal and watch the barges

effects.log: You watch the boatmen pole their barges. A long stroke down, a turn. It is the same sword.

events.text: Greenwood outlaws have robbed a grain barge on the Grand Canal under a Yue bridge, and the magistrate asks, very politely, whether the Yue still keep the canal or only write about it.

choices.text: Ride out after the outlaws

ok.log: You bring the grain back and the captain in ropes. The magistrate writes the house a letter of thanks.

fail.log: They melt into the reeds and leave you a bruise to remember them by.

choices.text: Write the magistrate a reply he will not forget

ok.log: Your reply is copied in every school in Shandong. The magistrate sends soldiers to the canal himself.

fail.log: Your reply is correct and very long. The magistrate does not finish it.

choices.text: Pay the barge owners from the house's own purse (20 taels)

effects.log: The house signs its name to the debt. The outlaws are a matter for another day.

events.text: The Taishan Sect comes down from the mountain for the Yue lecture day, when the scholars of the house read the classics aloud and the fist-masters of the mountain fall asleep on the benches.

choices.text: Give the lecture yourself

ok.log: Nobody falls asleep. The Taishan master thanks you with a bow as heavy as the mountain.

fail.log: Everyone falls asleep, the Taishan master first. He says it was the best sleep of his year.

choices.text: Spar with the Taishan disciples after

effects.log: Their fists are heavy and your sword is quick. Both sides learn something.

choices.text: Serve the tea and listen

effects.log: You hear the classics read by someone else, and understand them better.

events.text: The head of the Yue will name the heir by a written examination, as the founder did: one question, one night, one brush. The question is posted on the gate. It is about duty, and it is very hard.

choices.text: Sit the examination

ok.log: You answer in one unbroken page. The head of the house reads it aloud at the rite and names you heir.

fail.log: Your answer is honest and has one blot. A cousin's has none. You sign your name under the cousin's, as witness.

choices.text: Answer that duty would not compete for the seat

effects.log: The head of the house laughs for the first time in a year, and keeps your page.

choices.text: Do not sit, and grind the ink for those who do

effects.log: Every candidate writes with your ink. It is a kind of signature.

events.text: Every winter the Eon walk out onto the frozen river below their fortress and set a lantern on the ice for the old country beyond the sea. This year you carry the lantern for the first time, very carefully.

choices.text: Set it down where the ice is clearest

effects.log: Its light goes down into the river. The old people say it reaches Jinju. You believe them.

choices.text: Ask what the old country was like

effects.log: An aunt tells you of a river and a fortress on a cliff, very like this one. You decide to see it someday.

choices.text: Slide on the ice all the way back

effects.log: You fall, the lantern does not. The house says you have the Eon balance.

events.text: The Eon practise the Riverwall Sword on the fortress wall itself, one step from the drop to the ice. Aunt Ga-ram, the swordmistress, walks the wall with her eyes closed to show it can be done.

choices.text: Walk the wall through the whole form

ok.log: You finish on the last stone without a wobble. Aunt Ga-ram opens one eye and nods.

fail.log: You step back off the wall into a snowdrift. Aunt Ga-ram says the drift is why she chose that wall.

choices.text: Learn the old songs of the house from the guards

effects.log: They sing in the old tongue. You do not understand it yet, but the sword keeps the same time.

choices.text: Go with the ginseng hunters into the pines

effects.log: You come back with frost on your eyebrows and a root the size of your thumb.

events.text: Black Wind raiders have come over the pass to the border market and burnt three Eon stalls, and they left a message: foreigners hold no market in the north. The whole house turns to look at the sword hall.

choices.text: Ride for the pass before they cross back

ok.log: You catch them on the ice at the ford. The raiders go home with nothing, and the market opens the next day.

fail.log: They are more than you thought. You come back over the ice wounded, and they keep the pass.

choices.text: Rebuild the stalls in a day, in the open

effects.log: The market sees the Eon rebuild by nightfall. It is an answer too.

choices.text: Ask the White Wolf riders for help

effects.log: They come, and stay a week. The raiders do not come back this year.

events.text: White Wolf riders come in out of a blizzard to the Eon fortress, half frozen, as the two houses have always done for each other. Their leader asks for shelter, and for someone to ride with them in the spring.

choices.text: Promise to ride with them

effects.log: You swear it at the river, the Eon way. The wolves howl, and it sounds like agreement.

choices.text: Race their best rider across the ice when the storm clears

ok.log: You win by a length. The wolves give you a white fur, which they give to nobody.

fail.log: You lose by a length. The wolves laugh and give you a cup of something hot.

choices.text: Tend the frostbitten riders all night

effects.log: Nobody loses a finger. The pack does not forget.

events.text: The head of the Eon has gone out onto the river ice alone, as the founders did, to choose the heir. Whoever walks out to stand beside the head before dawn, and says nothing, will be heard.

choices.text: Walk out onto the ice and stand silent

ok.log: You stand until dawn without a word. The head of the house puts a hand on your shoulder: heir.

fail.log: The cold drives you back before dawn. A cousin stays. You bring her tea when she comes in.

choices.text: Light a lantern on the ice for the head instead

effects.log: The head of the house sees it and knows whose it is. It is not nothing.

choices.text: Keep the fortress gate till everyone comes in

effects.log: The gate stays open all night, and warm. Somebody has to.

events.text: At the last gate of the old wall, the Seomun give every child of the house a water-skin on its fourth spring, and send it to fill the skin of the first caravan through the gate. Today a long caravan comes in from the west.

choices.text: Fill the camel driver's skin first

effects.log: He bows to you as to a grown warden. The house says you know the old law.

choices.text: Fill the skin of the smallest child in the caravan

effects.log: She gives you a blue stone from very far away. You keep it all your life.

choices.text: Climb the camels instead

effects.log: You end up on the tallest one and have to be fetched down. The caravan laughs all the way to the oasis.

events.text: The Seomun practise the Sandwind Sabre on the dunes outside the gate, where the sand moves under every step. Aunt Yeo-wol, the sabre-warden of the house, sends a sandstorm of insults after anyone who falls.

choices.text: Cut the whole form on the moving dune

ok.log: The dune slides and you slide with it, sabre steady. Aunt Yeo-wol stops insulting you, which is a medal.

fail.log: You slide to the bottom of the dune in a cloud. The insults follow you all the way down.

choices.text: Watch how the wind moves the sand first

effects.log: The sabre should go where the sand goes. You see it in the ripples.

choices.text: Help the gate-keepers water the caravans

effects.log: You hear a dozen languages before noon, and learn to say thank you in four.

events.text: Riders of the Heavenly Demon Cult wait at the oasis below the gate, and their envoy demands that the Seomun close the road to any caravan the Cult has not taxed. He gives the house until sunset.

choices.text: Ride out at sunset and give him the answer with a sabre

ok.log: The envoy rides west without his banner. The road stays open, and every caravan carries the story.

fail.log: He is stronger than he looked. You come back to the gate bleeding, and it stays open only because it always has.

choices.text: Keep the gate open and stand in it, saying nothing

effects.log: The envoy waits until dark, then goes. The Seomun do not answer threats; they keep the gate.

choices.text: Send word to Kunlun and wait

effects.log: Kunlun answers in a week. By then the envoy has gone, and the caravans have waited.

events.text: Kunlun swordsmen come down from the western mountains to the Seomun gate every summer to trade snow lotus for salt and to tell the house what moves in the high passes. This year they ask you to guide them home.

choices.text: Guide them up the pass

ok.log: You bring them home a day early. The Kunlun abbot sends back a snow lotus with your name on the box.

fail.log: A rockfall turns you back halfway. The Kunlun go on alone, and wave from the ridge.

choices.text: Trade them salt for their news

effects.log: You hear what moves in the passes before anyone in the Central Plains does.

choices.text: Spar with their best swordsman at the gate

effects.log: Sabre and sword ring until dusk. You part sworn friends.

events.text: By the old law of the Seomun the heir is whoever keeps the gate alone for a whole night of sandstorm. The storm is coming over the dunes now, and the head of the house has hung the gate-key on its nail.

choices.text: Take the key and keep the gate

ok.log: At dawn the storm is gone and the gate is standing open, with you in it. The key is yours.

fail.log: The storm drives you in before midnight. A cousin takes the key out of your hand and goes back out.

choices.text: Keep the caravans inside safe through the storm

effects.log: Forty travellers and their camels sleep through it in the gate house. The old law has more than one gate.

choices.text: Sleep, and see who has the key in the morning

effects.log: Somebody does. The gate is open. The Seomun go on.

events.text: In Hubei the road passes the great hall of the Hwangbo Clan, and its gate stands open: the house takes in travellers with a name, and sometimes keeps them.

choices.text: Ask at the gate for an audience

ok.log: A steward brings you to the guest hall and the Hwangbo Clan gives you tea and a hearing. Your name goes into their books.

fail.log: The steward is polite and the gate is courteous, and the Hwangbo Clan is not at home to strangers today.

choices.text: Watch the young of the house practise in the yard

effects.log: You stand at the gate a while and watch the Hwangbo Clan train. Something of it stays with you.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: The road goes on. The hall watches you go.
